decisions.rationale: Verified: the section 4 table has 30 distinct primaries, and exactly the 10 listed objectives are secondary only. Section 4 says only the primary is reported. The collections-module-check practical's coding objectives (equals#o2, how-hashmap#o3, sorting#o1, grouping#o1, grouping#o3) and its two tasks include no loop-to-pipeline rewrite. Neither timed#o2 nor review#o2 is a practical objective. The 30/60 count is valid under the captain's rule (count chosen from coverage, no forced 45); what was wrong is the stated reason. Fix must achieve: section 7 states the real basis. Two reported items per taught topic is a design choice. The 10 secondary-only objectives are context, not reported. The larger alternative that reports all of them is named, with a true reason it was not chosen (uneven topic weighting). Section 5 says 'better assessed by writing or performance' instead of 'an MCQ cannot assess'. It drops the claim that the practical assesses review#o2, and describes timed#o2 as exercised only through the practical's time box. Blueprint itemCounts and durationMinutes stay 30/60. Status at the current plan: met (sections 5 and 7).

Verified bank titles in the stacks, lists, generics, sorting, method-references, grouping and lambdas banks, and the sorting page's null apply task (artifact.md line 76). Section 6 named none of them for q09, q16, q17, q18, q24, q26 or q28. I also found that q25 shares its shape with the lambdas bank's andThen and negate items. A word-overlap score cannot detect a shared structure. Fix must achieve: section 6 lists, for q09, q16, q17, q18, q24, q25, q26 and q28, the matching bank items and page tasks as 'must not repeat' entries. It records that the private author checks each item structurally (same mechanism plus same decision), not only by word overlap. An item that matches gains a second reasoning step or a cross-topic twist. Status at the current plan: met (section 6 structural rule and per-item entries).

Verified from the repo: the lists page teaches only best-effort ConcurrentModificationException for removal inside for-each, with Iterator.remove and removeIf as the safe forms. The wrapper page shows no remove call. No page teaches List.remove(int) against remove(Object), or index shifting. The planned q17 and q19 contexts invited exactly those untaught mechanics, which breaks section 4's taught-material rule. Fix must achieve: section 8 rules. No item depends on remove(int) versus remove(Object) overload resolution, index shifting or iterator internals. q17 keys the cause and the safe removal method, never an exact list of surviving elements. q19 locates boxing only through taught operations. The private author re-checks both items against these rules. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, untaught-list-mechanics rule). The follow-on second-step issue is education-d1. Same fix closes sme-c3.

Verified: review#o1 requires retrieval without notes, while the blueprint's allowedResources defers to the platform and names notes, course pages and the Java API documentation as possible resources. An item cannot enforce a closed-book condition, so reporting q30 against review#o1 was invalid as planned. Fix must achieve: no planned context or stem relies on a without-notes condition. q30 stays on review#o1 only if allowedResources states closed-book with course-owner confirmation. Otherwise q30's primary moves to an objective it measures that is not already a primary, and review#o1 is listed as untargeted with its reason. Sections 4 and 5, the count statements, and the blueprint's objectives and objectiveFormats change together. Status at the current plan: met. q30's primary is review#o2, review#o1 is untargeted with the notes reason, and the blueprint's objective set equals the 40-objective plan set (verified programmatically). Same fix closes sme-c10.

Verified: a count over authoring/catalog/collections-streams/**/topic.json gives 45 objectives, 3 of them on course-review/collections-and-streams-review-scenarios. The plan's 42 left these out without saying so. Fix must achieve: the counts say '42 taught-topic objectives' (or use 45 consistently), and section 5 accounts for the scenario page's three objectives with a reason. Status at the current plan: met (section 5, objective-reach list).

Verified: F28 in curriculum/snapshot/pep-calendar.json is a Review day. Section 7 gives its blocks as 120 minutes; the 60-minute MCQ plus the 30-minute practical, in place of the 45-minute block, gives 165. T14 (authoring/docs/tools/validators.md) sums topic budgets only. Fix must achieve: section 7 states 165 of 120 minutes and that T14 covers topic budgets only, not assessment time. Section 9 lists the extra 45 minutes as an open course-owner decision that release depends on. Status at the current plan: met (sections 7 and 9).

Verified: q29's planned context restated the timed#o3 objective text, including a spoken condition an MCQ cannot observe. Its objective pair mirrored q15's, and both contexts asked for a short problem plus its cost. Fix must achieve: q29 gets a concrete applied context that differs from q15. The spoken condition is dropped, and the plan records that the MCQ measures recognizing the complexity. q29 avoids the timed page's practised problems and the big-o repeated-value shape. Status at the current plan: met (section 4 q29 row, section 6).

Verified against the Java SE 25 API. HashMap and HashSet give no order guarantee, and groupingBy(Function) gives no guarantee about the Map type. List.sort documents no NullPointerException, so a null element fails only through a comparison. Section 8 scoped the order rule to q02/q03 and the null rule to q04, although q05, q22, q24, q28 and q30 rest on the same traps. The rule belongs in the plan, which binds the bank and any revision of it, whatever the current items do. Fix must achieve: the order rule applies to every item: hash-based and default groupingBy results are keyed on contents, sizes or get results only. The null rule extends to q24 (at least two elements and a comparison sure to reach the null, or key the nullsFirst/nullsLast repair). Status at the current plan: met (section 8, unspecified-order and nulls-in-sorting rules).

Verified: the wrapper page teaches that == between Integer objects is guaranteed only from -128 to 127, and that Java promises neither result outside that range. The equals page teaches that behavior after a stored key's compared field changes is unspecified. Section 8 had no rule binding q07 or q08 to these limits. Fix must achieve: q07 keys identity comparison guaranteed only from -128 to 127, with equals or unboxing as the repair, and never a definite result outside the range. q08 keys a compared-field change as unspecified behavior that can make lookup fail, never a guaranteed result, and keys an unrelated-field change as harmless. The private author confirms both authored keys follow this. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, integer-identity and mutated-key rules).

Verified: the same gap as education-c3. Under JLS 15.12.2.2 phase 1, an int argument on a wrapper-element list selects remove(int) without boxing, and no course page teaches that overload. I did not adopt the SME's alternative (a counted index loop that skips the shifted element), because index shifting is not taught either. Fix must achieve: the education-c3 rules, plus an explicit ban on passing an int-typed argument to remove on a wrapper-element list. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, untaught-list-mechanics rule).

Verified: the generics page teaches the ClassCastException only at a read into a String variable after an unchecked raw add. Where javac inserts the checked cast depends on the target type, and for some sites it depends on the compiler. Correction to the evidence: println of a String-typed element resolves to println(String) and does cast. The proposed rule is still sound and conservative. Fix must achieve: for q06 and q18, the failing read is placed only where the element must be a String, never at an Object target or in string concatenation. The raw call is keyed as compiling with an unchecked warning. Both are re-checked on the JDK 25 run. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, raw-types rule). The JDK 25 re-run is still pending under sme-c11.

Verified against the Java SE 25 API. String.toLowerCase() depends on the default locale, and equalsIgnoreCase folds case character by character, so an equals based on one and a hashCode based on the other can disagree. No course page teaches Locale. Normalizing once and then using equals and a hash on that one field keeps the contract in any locale. Fix must achieve: q21's stem limits values to ASCII letters. The keyed repair normalizes once and then uses equals and a hash on the normalized field. No option keys equalsIgnoreCase paired with a toLowerCase() hash as correct, and at most one valid repair appears. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, case-insensitive equality rule).

Verified: the stacks page never mentions the legacy Stack class's own exception types (0 hits). It teaches the legacy Stack class only through the documented prefer-Deque reason, and treats a null from poll/peek as 'empty' only because ArrayDeque rejects nulls. Section 8 gave the ArrayDeque null rule to q01 only, so q16 had no rule against relying on untaught Stack behavior. Fix must achieve: the ArrayDeque null rule extends to q16. Stack appears only for the documented prefer-Deque reason. No option, key or feedback relies on Stack's own exception types or claims a Stack null result. The private author applies this to q16. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, deques rule).

Verified: big-o-basics Activity 1 (nested-loop duplicate check, doubling multiplies the time by 4), Activity 3 (Mystery A) and the page's final check (Version B, one pass of TreeMap lookups) are close shapes to q20's planned growth-on-doubling context. A pure pairwise loop also does not use q20's secondary big-o#o1 (collection-operation costs). Separately, q08's planned context matches the equals page's Activity 3 (a compared-field change against an unrelated-field change on a stored key). Fix must achieve: q20's growth depends on one named collection operation's documented cost. Its shape differs from big-o Activities 1 and 3, the final check and the bank's hidden-contains loop. Section 6 adds every topic page's in-page activities and checks, with explicit entries for q20 and q08. Status at the current plan: see the second sme-c7 decision below.

Verified: no course page teaches that a TreeSet or TreeMap treats compare == 0 as the same element. Tie-breaking with thenComparing is taught, and grouping#o3 names both groupingBy and toMap with a merge function, so q23 and q28 could each have two defensible answers. Fix must achieve: q23 builds the tie loss from a repeated map key, with no valid tie-breaker option. q28 fixes the result shape, and every merge-function distractor visibly drops values. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, ties-and-duplicates rule).

Verified: the method-references page teaches the four reference kinds with non-ambiguous examples, and lambdas#o2 teaches the simplified one-abstract-method rule. Integer::toString as a Function<Integer,String> is overload-ambiguous and does not compile. Under JLS 9.8, an interface that redeclares a public Object method is still functional. Fix must achieve: every reference shown or keyed as valid compiles on JDK 25 and is not overload-ambiguous. No interface in an item redeclares a public Object method, so the taught rule and JLS 9.8 agree. Status at the current plan: met (section 8, method-references rule).

Verified: the same defect as education-c4 (review#o1's without-notes condition against an allowedResources that may permit notes). Fix must achieve: the education-c4 fix. Status at the current plan: met (q30 retargeted to review#o2, review#o1 untargeted with reason, blueprint objective lists consistent).

Verified: section 9 recorded the JDK 17.0.12 checks without a commit or run id, which authoring/AGENTS.md requires ('validated at <commit> by run <id>'). Section 8 promises Java SE 25 keys, but the checks ran on 17, and upload was not blocked on the JDK 25 re-run. Fix must achieve: section 9 records the JDK 17 run as 'validated at <commit> by run <id>' and keeps it marked as not Java SE 25 evidence. It blocks upload until the JDK 25 re-run (after the correction-loop rework) and the pilot timing are each recorded in that form. Status at the current plan: partly met. The run id and the upload block are recorded, but the commit is still pending ('named ... once committed'). The author must fill in the commit hash once this change is committed.

Verified against the current plan (sha256 af3cc2e33de1c72b9a139839f03385cd20418dba6098f7701bf5aed0c03e1136) and the banks. q17 now has lists#o3 as its secondary and a second step: predict the outcome on an unmodifiable factory list. That is taught: the lists page says any change to a List.of list throws UnsupportedOperationException. The section 8 removal rule requires an in-place change with one safe method among the options. q19 now adds 'predict how the code ends'. The section 6 q19 entry names the wrapper bank's spotting-unboxing item. But the q19 second step, a throw from unboxing a null read from a map into a primitive, is the same mechanism and decision as the wrapper bank item 'o2 - unboxing null', which section 6 does not name for q19 (it names it only for q07). Section 6 also still has two q17 entries; the older one gives only a new context and a distractor as its 'second step'. Fix must achieve: (1) section 6's q19 entry also names the wrapper bank's unboxing-null item, and q19's throw prediction sits inside a multi-call trace where the learner must first find which read unboxes a missing value, not a single-statement read. (2) The two q17 entries in section 6 merge into one that names the unmodifiable-fixture step. (3) q17's unmodifiable fixture contains at least one matching record. With no match, Iterator.remove is never called while removeIf still throws, so the outcome would depend on which safe method is keyed. The q17 Analyze label is acceptable now that it has two decisions.

Verified: Analyze is defined as 'diagnose a cause, separate two cases or compare near-miss alternatives' and Evaluate as 'choose and defend under competing needs'. The review page's translation activity (collections-and-streams-review artifact.md lines 13, 37, 67) is a loop-to-pipeline writing task. Status at the current plan: met. q30 is labelled Analyze and placed before the Evaluate block. Level totals are recounted as 9/15/6, which I verified from the section 4 table. Section 6 has a q30 entry naming the review page's translation activity, with q30 comparing near-miss pipelines that differ in one step each. Fix must achieve: what the current plan already states. Keep it with the section 8 equivalence rule (sme-d5).

Verified: in the reviewed version, q17, q19, q22 and q25 had no secondary, so the stated reason for leaving lists#o3 untargeted was false. Status at the current plan: met. lists#o3 is q17's secondary. The untargeted list is now timed#o2 and review#o1 only. Programmatically, the blueprint's objectives and objectiveFormats equal the 40-objective plan set (30 primaries and 10 secondary-only). Fix must achieve: what the current plan and blueprint already state.

Verified: in the reviewed version, 9 secondary-only objectives spanned 9 distinct topics, not 8. Status at the current plan: met after the education-d3 change. 10 secondary-only objectives span 10 distinct topics (programmatic check), and section 7 now says 10 topics weighted 3:2 over the other 5. Fix must achieve: what the current plan already states.

Verified: the earlier version of this record carried item-specific details supplied by the author's first brief. authoring/AGENTS.md forbids committing stems, options, keys and feedback. Fix must achieve: no rationale in this record quotes or paraphrases any item stem, option, key or feedback; rationales refer only to item ids, rule categories, plan sections and repo-verifiable facts. Every record that binds this file is re-hashed. Applied in this version: every rationale was rewritten, and the decisions and fix requirements are unchanged in substance. High severity: this closes only with a current SME recheck of this file marked resolved (T25).

Verified: JLS 15.12.2.6 makes the invocation type erased when unchecked conversion is needed for applicability. The generics page teaches inference only from type-safe arguments or the assignment target, so a raw-typed argument would key untaught behavior. Status at the current plan: met. The section 8 raw-types rule forbids passing a raw list straight to a generic method and requires q18 to pass a parameterized list polluted earlier through a raw alias, and the q18 row matches. Fix must achieve: what the current plan already states. The JDK 25 re-run must cover q18's compile-time and run-time expectations.

Verified against the Java SE 25 Map API: getOrDefault returns the default only when the key has no mapping, so a key mapped to null returns null and then fails to unbox. The wrapper page presents getOrDefault only as the safe read. Status at the current plan: met. Section 8 requires q19's stem to state that no key is mapped to null, so null can come only from a read of an absent key, and it counts getOrDefault's default argument as a boxing site. Fix must achieve: what the current plan already states.

Verified: the lists page teaches two equally safe forms (Iterator.remove and removeIf), and a reassigned stream result also 'removes' unless the same list object must change. Status at the current plan: met. The section 8 removal rule requires the stem to say the same list object must change in place, and allows only one safe removal method among the options. Fix must achieve: what the current plan already states, plus the matching-record fixture condition recorded under education-d1 so that the unmodifiable-list step has one outcome.

Verified against the Java SE 25 API: Stream.toList() returns an unmodifiable list, and List.sort and sorted() on an ordered stream are both stable, so stability cannot separate two options. Status at the current plan (af3cc2..., section 8 equivalence rule, reworded with the same meaning): met. Equivalent means the same elements in the same order. The stem explicitly sets list mutability aside. Every option sorts after the transformation, as the loop does. Section 6 says the near-miss pipelines differ in one step each. Fix must achieve: what the current plan already states. No separate stability rule is needed.

Second decision, at the current plan (sha256 af3cc2e33de1c72b9a139839f03385cd20418dba6098f7701bf5aed0c03e1136). The q20 context is now an indexed loop over a linked list whose growth on doubling comes from the cost of reaching an index, and the stem says which size doubles. Section 6 now forbids the big-o page's nested pairwise loop (Activity 1 and its prediction check), the single-operation cost listing (Activity 3 and the sorting activity) and the one-pass sorted-map lookup loop (Version B of the final check). This meets the recheck's requirement. Two value-free residuals, verified in the repo. (1) The big-o page (artifact.md lines 22 and 102) says LinkedList.get(i) is O(n) 'derived, not stated' from the documented traversal, while the q20 row says 'documented cost'. (2) The mechanism, a linear operation hidden inside a loop, is shared with the big-o bank's 'o3 - a hidden loop' item and the choosing-the-right-collection page's indexed-read prediction and step bench, although q20's decision (growth on doubling) differs. Fix must achieve: the q20 row says the cost is derived from the documented traversal, matching the page. Section 6's q20 entry also names the big-o bank's hidden-loop item and the choosing page's indexed-read prediction and step bench, and requires that q20's keyed decision is the doubling effect, not the complexity-and-fix decision or the choose-a-list decision. q08's section 6 entry (equals page's stored-key activity, plus the harmless-change contrast and the repair) meets the q08 part.

Verified at the current plan (sha256 4412b2f96bc6cfac68401b395153c8babeddd95928592bf636bb4a9f2eb79278): section 9 binds run cs-final-jdk17-20261109-r3 to 'this plan version' but names no commit. It forward-references a line that does not exist, so it does not yet meet the authoring/AGENTS.md form 'validated at <commit> by run <id>' that sme-c11 required. A commit cannot name its own hash, so the author's plan is acceptable: commit this change, then make an immediate follow-up commit that records the binding. That is the critic's own second remedy, and it continues sme-c11. The coverage md is evidence, not a T25 reviewable file (T25 binds only the course's assessment and lab files), so the follow-up does not invalidate critic coverage of the blueprint. Fix must achieve: (1) the follow-up commit replaces the 'named in the next line once committed' placeholder with 'validated at <first commit> by run cs-final-jdk17-20261109-r3', so no forward reference remains at the branch tip; (2) the named commit is one whose section 8 rules and section 4 contexts are the ones run r3 checked. If any item-affecting rule changed after r3, the author re-runs and names the new run; changes in wording only are recorded as 'rules unchanged in substance since run r3'; (3) the follow-up changes only that line and the regenerated course lock, still states JDK 17.0.12, and keeps the JDK 25 re-run and pilot timing as upload blockers; (4) both commits land on this branch before merge, so the merged plan never carries the placeholder.

Verified: after the education-d1 fix, q17 predicts the taught UnsupportedOperationException on an unmodifiable fixture (lists page artifact.md: List.of mutators throw it). The ConcurrentModificationException rule now reads 'not a ConcurrentModificationException', and the removal rule requires a matching record in the unmodifiable fixture so the removal is attempted. The two rules no longer conflict. Fix must achieve: what the current plan states. No rule may forbid q17's keyed unmodifiable-list outcome, and the CME rule stays limited to ConcurrentModificationException.

In the reviewed version, section 6's q20 entry still said 'documented cost' while the q20 row said 'derived'. Status at the current plan (sha256 4412b2f96bc6cfac68401b395153c8babeddd95928592bf636bb4a9f2eb79278): met. The section 6 q20 entry now says the growth comes from the cost of one named collection operation, 'derived from that operation's documented traversal', which agrees with the q20 row's 'derives from the documented walk from the nearer end'.
